LESSON: DATA INTERPRETATION (GROUPED DATA)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: DATA HANDLING AND PROBABILITY
Topic 5.1: Data Interpretation (Grouped Data)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Data Interpretation (Grouped Data), part of DATA HANDLING AND PROBABILITY in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we interpret data? 2. How do we determine the median of a grouped data from a real life situation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Data Interpretation (Grouped Data) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner develops independence as they collect, organise and interpret data.

● Communication and collaboration: The learner contributes to group decision making as they discuss and determine the

modal class, mean and median of grouped data.

● Digital literacy: The learner develops interaction with technology as they use digital or other materials to determine the

mean and median of grouped data.

Values:
Respect: The learner enhances patience as they work together in groups to collect data from the immediate environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Citizenship: The learner develops responsibility as they collect data that may relate to the population.

● Education for Sustainable Development (ESD): A learner develops life skills as they choose career paths in statistics and

other related fields.

Link to other subjects:

● Integrated Science: The learner interprets data related to different organisms and materials.

● Social Studies: The learner analyses and interprets data in different social aspects.
